feedback.correct: The quantifier 'both' is used to refer to two things or people together.
The quantifier 'no' is used to indicate a lack of something.
The quantifier 'many' is used to refer to big quantities.

instruction.text: Match the definitions to the correct quantifiers.

atoms.sound: some, refers to an unknown quantity, typically positively

atoms.b: refers to an unknown quantity, typically negatively, and is also used in questions
atoms.sound: any, refers to an unknown quantity, typically negatively, and is also used in questions

instruction.text: Create a sentence using the words. Remember to use the correct quantifier.
Fill in the gap with the correct quantifier.

atoms.a: ssml: How, <break time='500ms'/> people were there at the concert?
atoms.b: How ((++many some)) people were there at the concert?

atoms.a: ssml: Vic has two dogs, <break time='500ms'/> of them are Jack Russel Terriers.
atoms.b: Vic has two dogs, ((++both all)) of them are Jack Russell Terriers.
